claim_text: JPAIS is structured as a clinical AI auditability and governance framework.

JPAIS consists of Jurisprudential Grounding, Pre-Deployment Safety Validation, Algorithmic Transparency & Attestation, Interaction & Physician Oversight Thresholds, Surveillance/Drift/Circuit Breakers, and MED-REF.
The framework proposes evidentiary transaction binding and auditability across clinical AI lifecycle events.
JPAIS proposes formal pre-deployment safety validation before clinical AI deployment.
The framework proposes validation against defined clinical safety and performance criteria before deployment.
The framework proposes shadow-mode operation before higher-risk clinical deployment.
The framework proposes evaluation of model behavior under distribution shift and out-of-distribution conditions.
The framework proposes clinical failure-mode analysis as part of deployment safety governance.
The framework references HFMEA/FMEA-style methods for clinical AI risk analysis.
JPAIS proposes explainability mechanisms for clinical AI outputs.
The source identifies SHAP as an explainability technique.
The source identifies Grad-CAM as an explainability technique for relevant model architectures.
JPAIS proposes cryptographic provenance and attestation for AI lifecycle evidence.
The source references HMAC-SHA256, TPM 2.0 and X.509-based identity/provenance controls.
JPAIS proposes explicit physician oversight thresholds for clinical AI systems.
The framework proposes differentiated autonomy levels according to clinical risk.
The source defines Tier 1 as informative/low-risk AI assistance.
The source defines Tier 2 as collaborative/high-risk AI assistance requiring greater human oversight.
The source describes Tier 3 as autonomous execution/critical-risk AI and states that such autonomy should be prohibited for diagnostics, prescriptions and emergency triage.
JPAIS proposes post-deployment surveillance of clinical AI systems.
The framework proposes monitoring for model drift.
The framework references PSI and KL-divergence-style statistical monitoring for distribution changes.
The framework references Mahalanobis-distance/out-of-distribution monitoring.
The framework proposes circuit breakers or controlled shutdown/escalation mechanisms when defined safety conditions are exceeded.
The source references a 99th-percentile threshold for certain out-of-distribution monitoring.
The source references PSI >= 0.25 as a monitoring threshold.
The source references COR >= 0.30 as a monitoring threshold.
The source references a 3–5 second delay threshold in a clinical AI safety context.
The source references a 60–90 day shadow-mode period.
Permenkes No. 24 Tahun 2022 is an Indonesian regulation concerning medical records and is currently listed as in force by JDIH BPK.
KMK No. HK.01.07/Menkes/1423/2022 concerns guidelines for variables and metadata in electronic medical record implementation.
UU No. 27 Tahun 2022 is the Indonesian Personal Data Protection Law and identifies health data/information as specific personal data.
SE Menkominfo No. 9 Tahun 2023 concerns AI ethics and provides ethical principles and responsibilities for relevant AI actors/PSEs.
SE Menkominfo No. 9 Tahun 2023 includes responsibility guidance stating that AI should not be organized as a policy determinant and/or decision-maker concerning humanity.

The source's bundled Indonesian regulatory discussion establishes specific clinical AI liability, retention, governance and decision-making requirements across Permenkes 24/2022, UU PDP, SE 9/2023 and UU 17/2023.

The source incorrectly states that Article 39 of Permenkes No. 24 Tahun 2022 establishes a five-year minimum retention period. The corrected requirement is a minimum of 25 years from the last patient visit.
Under Article 25 of Permenkes No. 24 Tahun 2022, the medical record document belongs to the healthcare facility, which is responsible for loss, damage, falsification and unauthorized use.
Under Article 26, the contents of the medical record belong to the patient.
Permenkes No. 24 Tahun 2022 contains provisions concerning electronic signatures for security/protection and verification/authentication of electronic medical records and signer identity.
SE Menkominfo No. 9 Tahun 2023 contains principles including inclusivity, humanity, security, accessibility, transparency, credibility/accountability and personal data protection.
The claim that SE Menkominfo No. 9 Tahun 2023 is equivalent in legal status to an Act of Parliament and independently establishes statutory medical AI prohibitions is unsupported.
SE Menkominfo No. 9 Tahun 2023 can be cited as an Indonesian AI ethics and policy guidance reference.
UU No. 17 Tahun 2023 is an Indonesian health-sector law relevant to the broader health technology and health information context.
Specific provisions of UU No. 17 Tahun 2023 establish the precise clinical AI liability model described in JPAIS-MED-REF.
The source references HL7 FHIR R4 and HL7 CQL as interoperability and clinical data technology references.
The source references NIST, ISO/IEC, SWGDE and related standards and frameworks.
The source identifies specific legal, technical and GIS topics as requiring additional research.
